item.title: Human activity more than doubles Arctic fire occurrence, satellite analysis suggests
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Fires in the Arctic are not solely a regional issue, as shown by the hazy skies in Switzerland last summer despite otherwise sunny weather. Smoke from major fires in northern Canada crossed the Atlantic and reached Europe. Until now, large-scale studies of Arctic tundra fires have focused primarily on rising temperatures and drought as the main drivers.

item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Can a crack be supersonic? Can the fracture that triggers an avalanche propagate faster than the limiting velocity predicted by classical fracture mechanics? The question remains the subject of debate within the scientific community. While some numerical and experimental studies suggest that avalanche cracks may propagate at supersonic speeds, others offer a different interpretation.
